item: Two whole-table counts that sat inside a statement deadline which could not stop them now loop (count(id) for the Library figures keyword_mentions count, count(1) for the content-share estimate); the sweep that found them is filed, with three stated limits
refs: PR #1563; audit 0.5.0; R309; deadline-bound sweep S1 S2
summary: From the WAL lane's deadline-bound sweep (R309): statement_deadline is a progress handler asked once per 20,000 VM opcodes, and a bare count(*) is one opcode, so a deadline around it bounds nothing. S1: the Library figures' background keyword_mentions count (src/api/database.py), whose 300 s deadline is documented as protecting the pooled connection and the read snapshot the count holds, ran whole under a 1e-6 s deadline over 1,240,657 mentions; it is now count(id) (same number: id is the primary key), which raises the typed timeout. THE HOLD IT SHORTENS: the connection and the WAL-pinning read snapshot the count holds, which lasted as long as the count did and is now cut at the 300 s; it is one of the long holds the A-029 swap-window hold-bound question concerns (swap_window has no timer on the hold), and no bound for that window is proposed here. THE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: the 300 s deadline is now live for this count (before, it never fired, so a count needing more than 300 s finished and was carried; now it is stopped at 300 s and the figure stays failed for 900 s before a retry, as the deadline was documented to do); whether a field corpus reaches 300 s on count(id) is not measured. S2: content_share_estimate (src/monitoring/storage.py), the encrypted store's normal path because neither qualified sqlcipher3 build has dbstat, counted articles with a bare count(*) under a docstring that said it was bounded by the deadline; it is now count(1), and the docstring says what the deadline does and does not bound (the probes after the count are 400 runs of one short statement, bounded by their own number: the handler's opcode counter belongs to a prepared statement, so 400 runs of that probe text ran whole under a 1e-6 s deadline and 4,000 raised, while 4,000 distinct short statements ran whole). Figures name their statement (300,000 articles, 1,240,657 mentions, the app's SQLCipher 4.12.0 engine, 5 cold runs): the mentions count 93 ms median cold before, 135 ms after (warm 1.0 to 44.7 ms); the articles count 41 ms cold before, 50 ms after (warm 0.6 to 6.2 ms); the price is warm CPU only at this size, not measured above 1.24 M mentions, and the 43/55/182 s figures in the code comments were taken on the bare statement (superseded, pending). Tests: tests/test_deadline_bound_statements.py, the real deadline at 1e-6 over 30,000 rows, red against each statement respelled as a bare count(*). Stated limits, no PR (four): an FTS phrase query's iterator set-up is uninterruptible (90 to 127 ms here); PRAGMA quick_check/integrity_check have an uninterruptible page-walk unit (about 0.3 ms per MiB warm); verify.py's Stop answers after 1.3 to 1.5 s at its 100,000-opcode interval. The fourth (R312) is the six per-table bare counts of database_stats (src/api/database.py:140, the _COUNTED_TABLES loop) that a second recording over all 57 bundle members found in performance.json: attributed by statement identity, not by a call stack; left bare because the Database tab's served-cache route has no deadline of its own, so count(1) there would charge every refresh the loop form's CPU for a stop only the bundle member's 300 s deadline could use; the sizes of article_links and article_mentioned_dates on a field corpus are not measured; the recorder's own limits are a 15 MiB store, four members that ran no statement (ai-runs, ai, country-code-duplicates, home-cards), and members that open their own connection being invisible to it. The FK-check figure (R312; statement PRAGMA foreign_key_check, whole database, three encrypted synthetic stores through the app's SQLCipher 4.12.0 engine, cold = file evicted and a fresh process, 5 rounds, median; the host's disk cache may still be warm): 300,000 articles with 1,240,657 mentions 5.4 s cold (3.4 s warm), 120,000 articles with 2,244,329 mentions 2.4 s (2.1 s), 300,000 articles with 9,900,000 mentions 11.0 s (9.7 s), the whole corpus_integrity report 8.8 s, 4.9 s and 24.7 s cold against its shared 60 s deadline; keyword ids were skewed in the first two stores and uniform in the third; the earlier 6 microseconds per child row per FK arithmetic (240 s at 20 M mentions) is superseded, 6 microseconds having been a per-ARTICLE-row figure (5.2 to 6.0 per article in all three), and the mention check cost 0.66 to 1.65 microseconds per mention warm; nothing was measured above 9.9 M mentions or 300,000 articles and no timeout is claimed. Routed: the diagnostics bundle's COUNT(*) FROM keyword_mentions to RC2, the unfiltered law_documents count to Export; fts.py:1348 and integrity.py:243 stay R299 stated limits.
